clue.text: Justify former suggestion to pen Sun's leader …

parts.note: ex is the usual prefix or word for a former partner or holder

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, so the suggestion goes round the next letter

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint given to an actor

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of the word Sun's

explanation.surface: Someone defends a past proposal, the ellipsis leading on into the next clue about the Sun newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse a fault is to justify or explain it away, a verb-for-verb synonym.

clue.text: Yale is broken with little effort

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Yale lock that is broken easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yale is' reads as subject and verb, but 'is' joins the fodder: the letters of YALE IS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily means without strain, with little effort.

clue.text: Make do on street without sharp turning

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them, to con them

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the street goes round the next part
turning means the word for sharp is read backwards

parts.note: curt means sharp or brusque in speech

explanation.surface: Advice to make do on a street, avoiding any sharp turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make do' looks like one phrase, but Make is the definition and do gives CON.
explanation.definitionFit: To construct something is to build or make it.

clue.text: Support for rider's foot wearing spur?

definitions.text: Support for rider's foot wearing spur?

indicators.note: wearing means the spur word is worn around the next letter

parts.note: to spur on is to stir up or incite

indicators.note: a word's foot is its last letter, here of rider's

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a rider's spurred boot rests in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer, while 'rider's foot' also supplies R, the foot of the word rider, inside STIR UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the loop hanging from a saddle that supports a rider's foot, and a spurred boot sits in it.

clue.text: … Sun accepts also end of naked model

indicators.note: a word that accepts another takes it inside itself

parts.note: the Sun is a star
and means also, in addition

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word naked

explanation.surface: Continuing from the ellipsis, the Sun tabloid seems to take on a nude model.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the two clues as one tabloid sentence; the Sun here is the star, not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a model or exemplar against which others are measured.

clue.text: Inordinately large instrument

parts.note: too means excessively, inordinately
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A description of an oversized musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is an implement, an instrument used for a job.

clue.text: Most open new undergarment clothes top

indicators.note: clothes means the new garment dresses the next part, going round it

parts.note: a vest is an undergarment in British usage
A1 means first-rate, top, written here with I for the 1

explanation.surface: A fashion note about new underwear worn over a top, revealing as much as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, top quality, appears as AI, the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The naivest person is the most unguarded and trusting, the most open in that sense.

clue.text: Prevent state terrorism's source

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: source picks the first letter, where the word terrorism's begins

explanation.surface: A plea to stop the state from being the source of terrorism.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a danger is to ward it off, to prevent it.

clue.text: Blow from behind is astern

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A nautical observation that a wind blowing from behind comes from astern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow from behind' reads as a tail wind, but Blow is the definition, and the answer runs through behind is astern.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a sudden misfortune or setback, a calamity.

clue.text: Small, dark and bright

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
unlit means without light, dark

explanation.surface: A description of something, perhaps a room, that is small, dark and bright, a contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere sunlit is lit by the sun and so bright.

clue.text: Seams seen in short stockings? Goodness!

indicators.note: seen in places the seams inside the shortened stockings
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: hose is a collective word for stockings
the seams on stockings are lines running up the back

explanation.surface: An exclamation at seeing the seams on old-fashioned stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiness is saintliness or moral virtue, a synonym for goodness; both also work as mild oaths.

clue.text: Speech elongated keeping level

indicators.note: keeping means the words hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A drawn-out speech that keeps an even tone.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or rank in an organisation.

clue.text: Learning to be saucy following diet?

indicators.note: following means the saucy word comes after the diet word

parts.note: lite is the spelling used on diet or low-calorie products
racy means risqué, saucy

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about whether eating lightly leads to being saucy.
explanation.definitionFit: Literacy is learning in the sense of education, being able to read and write.

clue.text: Deliveries, reportedly, for docks

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like the one just defined

parts.note: a delivery in a maternity ward is a birth

explanation.surface: Reads like a news report about deliveries arriving at the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: Berths are the moorings at a quayside where ships dock.

clue.text: Practically excellent friend for ever

indicators.note: practically means almost, so the word lacks its last letter

parts.note: fine means excellent, of high quality
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A declaration of a near-perfect friend for life.
explanation.definitionFit: Finally, as in once and finally, means conclusively and for good, so for ever.

clue.text: Abrupt decline, possibly becoming erratic

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the phrase might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A steep, sudden fall, maybe in a market, turns out to be erratic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpredictable behaves erratically, without a pattern.

clue.text: Insect runs around top of orange plants

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: around means the runs word goes round the next letter

parts.note: trots are jogging runs

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word orange

explanation.surface: An insect scurrying round the top of an orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroots are root vegetables, the plants grown for their red roots.

clue.text: Great acting performed about return of Private Ryan?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next part
performed means worked through or done afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as letters to rearrange

indicators.note: return of means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a GI is a US soldier, as in the film Saving Private Ryan

explanation.surface: Praise for the acting in the war film Saving Private Ryan.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means enormous, great in size.

clue.text: Worried, I got nervier at questioning

indicators.note: worried means agitated and shaken up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone admits growing anxious while being questioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Interrogative means asking questions, as in an interrogative look or sentence.

clue.text: End dimensions' limits admitting time slows down

indicators.note: admitting means the end word lets the next letter in

parts.note: the rear is the back end

indicators.note: limits picks the outer letters of the word dimensions'

explanation.surface: Technical prose about the boundaries of measurements and time slowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Retards means delays or slows the progress of something.

clue.text: This compiler's exercise catching innocent in deadlock

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so this compiler's means I am

indicators.note: catching means the exercise letters hold the next word

parts.note: PE is physical exercise, as in school PE lessons
an ass is a gullible innocent, a simpleton

explanation.surface: The setter describing a PE class trapping an innocent in a stalemate.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a position from which no progress is possible, a deadlock.

clue.text: A year taking course leads to indifference

indicators.note: taking means the first part takes in the next word

parts.note: a path is a course or route

explanation.surface: A year spent on a course of study ends in boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is lack of interest or concern, indifference.

clue.text: Related a passage including start of novel

indicators.note: including means the passage word holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a gate is a passage or way through, as at an airport

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the word novel

explanation.surface: A related passage from the opening of a novel, as if in a literature essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnate means related through the father's line, kin on the male side.

clue.text: More current needs electricity with extra resistance initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: An electrician's remark that a current needs extra resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' and 'resistance' suggest electricity, but current here means up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Newer means more recent, more up to date or current.

clue.text: Conservative facing constituent crony rejected nonsense

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: a constituent is a part of the whole
a crony is a pal or close friend

explanation.surface: A Tory MP dismissing a voter's political pal as talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk, nonsense meant only to win applause.

clue.text: Single, going round clubs in the past

indicators.note: going round means the single word encloses the next letter

parts.note: one means single
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A single person who used to go round the nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time in the past.

clue.text: Magnificent until group covers Queen

parts.note: to means until, as in nine to five

indicators.note: covers means the group word goes round the queen

parts.note: a wing is a group or faction within a party
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Praise of something magnificent until a band covers a song by the rock group Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Towering means outstanding or lofty in stature, so magnificent in a figurative sense.

clue.text: Company, commonly the man's company, right?

indicators.note: commonly marks a dropped aitch in common or Cockney speech

parts.note: the man's means he is, shortened to he's

explanation.surface: A Cockney asking whether a business is the man's own firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' drops the H, giving 'E'S as a Cockney would say it. The first Company is the definition, the second gives CO.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a companion, someone who keeps a person company; the escort as a group of guards is also a company.

clue.text: Name of church started around mid-century

indicators.note: around means the started word sits on either side of the next letter

parts.note: risen means got up, started up

indicators.note: mid picks the middle letter of the word century

explanation.surface: A church's name that dates from the middle of a century.
explanation.definitionFit: To christen a baby or a ship is to give it a name, often in a church ceremony.

clue.text: Tough as iron facing one's gutless temerity

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
one's is a contraction of one is

indicators.note: gutless means the word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A boast of being tough as iron, against someone whose temerity lacks guts.
explanation.definitionFit: Feisty means spirited and combative, so tough in a scrappy way.
